ski-1.name: Ski · Red
ski-1.guidance:
LEVEL 1 - RED


I am just learning to ski. | Goal: Turn Both Ways and Stop
Mobility
   Play Games with boots only
I can put on, take off and carry my own skis.
    Knows how bindings work
    Knows how to clean off boots
    Keeps fingers away from bindings
I can walk with my skis on. (S&B)
    Can walk on flat terrain in a square
    Slide with one leg in the air
I am able to side-step up the hill. (E)
    Can side-step up gentle slope
    Can roll edge over using ankle
    Can keep skis parallel while stepping
I am able to snowplow to a gentle stop.
    Balanced position with hands out in front
    Skis flat, no extreme edge
    Can maintain snowplow position
I am able to get up with minimal assistance.
    Knows to turn skis across the hill
    Can get up with skis on
I can turn in both directions. (T&P)
    Good turn shape
    Skis turn together in a wedge
I can stay balanced and show good body position at all times.
    Hands in front
    Head up where you are going
    Knees bent/feel front of the boot
    Not too far backwards or forwards

rows.label: Mobility: move in boots
I can put on, take off & carry my skis
I can walk with my skis on
I am able to sidestep uphill
I am able to snowplow to a gentle stop
I am able to get up with minimal assistance
I can turn in both directions
I can stay balanced & show good body position

ski-2.name: Ski · Green
ski-2.guidance:
LEVEL 2 - GREEN


I can turn both ways and stop. | Goal: Control Speed Using Turn Shape
I can turn around the features in the learning area.
    Able to avoid obstacles (S&B)
    Uses turn shape to control speed
    Is in control
    Starting to do hops in traverse between turns
    Linking turns

I am able to follow my instructor in a line. (P.C, T)
    Can follow directions
    Able to stop at will
    Does not pass others

I can stop using behind and below.
    Slows down before getting close to the group
    Leaves space between themselves and others

I can control my speed and stop by turning uphill. (T&P)
    Turning across the fall line and back up the hill
    Could try hockey stops
I can ski green runs comfortably & match my skis near end of the turn. (E)
    Uses wide stance
    Reinforce with lots of practice on comfortable terrain
    Minimum terrain = maximum performance

I am able to link turns on green slopes to control my speed.
    Speed is controlled by turn shape, not snowplow
    Does not take up too much of the run

I can get up on my own.
    Skis are downhill from hips and pointed across the fall line
I can stay balanced skiing over a bump.
    Kids should not be getting air at this level
    Have good form while adjusting to small bumps or rolls over flat terrain

rows.label: I can turn around features
I am able to follow my instructor in a line
I can stop using behind & below
I can control my speed & stop by turning uphill
I can ski green runs comfortably
I am able to link turns on green runs to control my speed
I can get up on my own

ski-3.name: Ski · Blue
ski-3.guidance:
LEVEL 3 - BLUE


I can control speed using turns on green terrains.
Goal: Ski with control with a wide parallel stance with poles on blue runs.

I can adapt my turn shape to control speed on varied terrain.
    Can do a mixed radius run - 3 short, 3 long, 3 medium
    Looks ahead - adjusts to pitch of slope and maintains speed
    Round, shallow turns

I can maintain an athletic stance while holding my poles in front.
     Arms up, ahead of the body

I am able to ski all green runs using wide-stance parallel turns. (P.C)
    No stem to start the turn
    Can adjust to different snow conditions
    Minimum terrain = maximum speed
    Well balanced body position - arms ahead, eyes up, knees bent

I can skate on flat and gentle slopes. (S&B)
    Play a game: Relay, Follow the Leader
    Kick and glide
    Use as a warm up any time

I can side slip on both sides for 4 metres on groomed terrain. (E)
    Slide at a constant speed
    Slide with good balance
    Can adjust edge angle with the ankle joint and lower leg
    Skis remain parallel
    Edge set to flat ski

LEVEL 3 - BLUE



I am able to do hockey stops on both sides. (E, T&P)
    Can turn both skis without stemming at the start
    Able to come to come to a complete stop
    Adjusts lateral balance to avoid falls on inside
    Able to stop on a straight line


I can ski up a side bank and turn back down.
    How to identify a safe side bank (begin with small banks)
    Work on edge control to climb
    Adjust to terrain changes
    Look in travel direction
    Turn head and shoulders


I can ski blue runs with a parallel stance.
    Very confident and consistent
    Can adjust to different snow conditions
    Reinforce through mileage on appropriate terrain


I understand how to merge and who has the right of way.
    Alpine responsibility code
    Look uphill before merging


READY FOR DEVO PROGRAM

rows.label: I can adapt turn shape to control my speed
I maintain an athletic stance while my poles are in front
I am able to ski all green runs in wide parallel stance
I can skate on flat gentle terrain
I can sideslip both sides 4 meters on groomed runs
I am able to do hockey stops on both sides
I can ski up a side bank & back down
I understand who has the right of way & how to merge

ski-4.name: Ski · Black
ski-4.guidance:
LEVEL 4 - BLACK


I am able to ski parallel turns on blue runs while holding poles in front.
Goal: Improve edging skills, pole plant and ski parallel on black runs in a
variety of snow conditions.

I can make large curved turns on green terrain. (T&P)
    Speed is appropriate
    Aware of other skiers/riders on the hill


I can maintain my balance and link parallel turns on blue runs in varied
terrain. (S&B, P.C)
    Adjusts balance and pressure as necessary for varied terrain
    Adjusts turn shape as necessary for varied terrain


I can make 15 fall-line short-radius turns on blue runs. (T&P, T)
    Able to maintain a constant speed
    Consistent pole plant
    Link consistent turns - no stopping


I am able to ski with round parallel turns on black runs.
    Adapts turn size to suit terrain
    Rounded, rhythmic turns
    Show good body position


I make solid pole plants with proper timing and coordination.
    Wears pole strap properly
    Knows where and when to plant the pole in different turns
    Stating to keep the pole baskets continuously moving
    Plants pole to initiate the turn and stabilize the upper body
    Adjusts the position of pole plant in relation to steepness, terrain
    and type of turn
    Steep slope/short radius - plant further downhill in fall-line

LEVEL 3 - BLACK


I am comfortable with speed on groomed terrain.
    Demonstrates control and awareness of others of the hill
    Proper technique and body position is still shown
    Tuck drills & short radius turns


I can safely pick my own line down blue runs and choose a safe
stopping location.
    Able to read terrain and identify hazards
    Speed is appropriate for terrain
    Talk about hazards and when going fast is not ok


I am able to carve turns on blue runs. (E).
    Demonstrates edging at the fall line
    Uses lower leg to obtain edge

rows.label: I can make large carved turns on green terrain
I can maintain balance, link parallel turns on blue runs
I can make 15 fall line short radius turns on blue runs
I am able to ski round, parallel turns on black runs
I make pole plants with proper timing & coordination
I am comfortable with speed on groomed terrain
I can pick my own line on blue runs & find a safe stop location
I am able to carve turns on blue runs

ski-5.name: Ski · Double Black
ski-5.guidance:
LEVEL 5 - DOUBLE BLACK

I am able to ski strong parallel turns on black runs. I enjoy skiing difficult
terrain and conditions.
Goal: Improve edging, pressure control, timing and coordination in varied
terrain and conditions
I can perform short radius turns on black runs.
    Edging occurs at or near the fall line
    Consistent speed maintained > Speiss
    Able to keep skis on the snow throughout the turn
I am comfortable with speed on all black runs.
    Control and awareness of other skiers/riders are demonstrated
    at all times
    Proper technique and body position is still shown
I can carve on groomed runs and steeps.
    Edging phase is consistently at or above the fall line
    Maintain consistent speed
    Able to adjust turn shape as terrain changes
I can link a series of controlled switch turns on groomed green terrain.
    Able to ski fluidly with little or no stopping
    Balanced on outside ski
    Looking over outside shoulder
    Speed is appropriate
    Do not take up too much of the run
I am able to keep a consistent rhythm in short radius turns.
    Turn size is appropriate
    Well-timed pole plant
    Able to complete their turns
I am comfortable with higher speeds on all terrain and in varied snow
conditions.
    Adjusts balance and pressure
    Adjusts turn shape and speed as necessary for varied terrain
    Can choose a suitable line by looking ahead/planning

rows.label: I can perform short radius turns on black runs
I am comfortable with speed on all black runs
I can carve on groomed runs & steeps
I can link a series of switch turns on groomed green runs
I am able to keep a consistent rhythm in short-radius turns
I am comfortable with higher speeds on all terrain & in varied snow conditions

snowboard-1.name: Snowboard · Red
snowboard-1.guidance:
LEVEL 1 - RED


Learn to use equipment.
    Knows parts of the board
    Front, Back, Toe, Heel, Bindings
    Attach front foot while standing
Learn to move around on flat terrain.
Skating
    Eyes forward
    Weight on front foot
    Body oriented with length of board
    Small steps
Develop balance while sliding.
Straight Running
    Small, gradual slope experiment with putting back foot on
    the board & gliding
    SR with toe and heel drag
Gas Pedal
    Board across hill
    Slightly increase toe or heel edge
    Experiment with back foot against back binding
Develop confidence with both feet attached.
    Attach back foot; try while standing
    Practice sideslipping
Learn to control speed.
    Sideslip toe side
    Sideslip heel side
Learn to control direction.
    Pendulum heel side
    Pendulum toe side turn head to see direction of travel
    Resist turning the body

rows.label: I know my equipment
I can move around on flat terrain
I have good balance while sliding
I can slide with both feet attached
I can control my speed, sideslip
I can control my direction, pendulum

snowboard-2.name: Snowboard · Green
snowboard-2.guidance:
LEVEL 2 - GREEN


Practice controlling speed and direction.
Power Pendulum (Pivots)
    Rotate hips and knees into fall line
    Accentuate rotation of board towards fall line, creating an arced path
    Reverse movement to rotate out of fall line to control speed
Garland Exercise
    Increase speed
    Rotate in opposite direction
    Turn Board Back Up Hill
    "Chicken Turns"
Learn to turn the snowboard.
    Heelside turns with assistance
    Toeside turns with assistance
    Flex hips, knees and ankles
    Maintain alignment in the upper body with feet
    Weight centered over both feet and sideslip to control speed
Increase balance and stability.
    Toeside and heelside turns without assistance
    Link the turns with a gentle traverse between
    Keep legs and ankle flexed after the fall line
    Eyes forward in the direction of the new turn
Safety on the Hill.
    Look into uphill traffic
    Lifts: Learn how to load (skate up)
    Unload straight run with toe/heel drag
Learn to control speed.
    On steeper terrain, make smaller, rounder turns (increase pivot
    movement)
    Follow the leader
    Sliding 180s & 360s
    Tail presses on flat terrain

rows.label: I can control my speed & direction
I can turn with assistance, heelside/toeside
I can use balance & stability to link turns on a gentle slope
I know hill safety: three points of alpine code
I can control the speed with pivot movements on steeper terrain

snowboard-3.name: Snowboard · Blue
snowboard-3.guidance:
LEVEL 3 - BLUE


Develop balance and steering skills.
Maintain a relaxed body position
    Experiment with position and balance tactics
    Focus on maintaining the relaxed position
    Sliding 360s
    Hopping in traverse
    Mini-motorboat turns (alignment)
    Use knees and feet to help make smaller turns
    Lower body rotation and steering skills will decrease the size of turns
    Pivot-related tactics will help
    Headlight on knees
    Garland/fall line pivot
    Focus on using knees and feet to guide the board
    Riding with restricted arms


Increase edge control.
Carved Traverse/Pencil Lines
    Pure edge/new sensation
    Carve traverse on flats, low speed
    Maintain equal weight over feet or slightly over back foot
    Spraying snow to the sides of the run
    Will use the edge earlier in the turn
    Will help develop bend in the board and rounder turn shape


I gain comfort at higher speeds.
Can link medium-sized turns in varied terrain
    Use skills of lower body rotation, steering
    Make turn size corridor smaller than used to

LEVEL 3 - BLUE



I gain comfort at higher speeds.
Can link medium-sized turns in varied terrain
    Use skills of lower body rotation, steering
    Make turn size corridor smaller than used to


Experiment with switch riding.
Can link switch turns on green terrain
    Start with beginner turn but in switch position


Learn new flatland tricks.
Can perform a nose and tail press
    Moving hips down for stability then back over tail or forward over
    nose
    Flat-based glide to presses in an edged traverse
Pop off both feet
    Static hops to pop while moving
    Understands alpine responsibility code - 3 points



** can only have two learning (all other skills mastered)
in order to pass and move to the next level

rows.label: I can maintain a relaxed body position
I can carve traverse/pencil lines
I can link medium-sized turns in varied terrain
I can link switch turns on green terrain
I can perform a nose & tail press
I can ride the chair lift without assistance
I know the alpine code

snowboard-4.name: Snowboard · Black
snowboard-4.guidance:
LEVEL 4 - BLACK


Increase edge control.
Maintains balance as the terrain gets steeper and speed increases
    Position and balance tactics
    Maintain a relaxed body
    Sliding 360s
Short radius turns on blue and black
    Lower body rotation
    Steering skills
    Pivot and timing tactics
    Headlight on knees
    Spray the snow to trees
    Sideslip to short radius turns
Carved turns
    Pencil lines on green terrain


Gain more comfort at higher speeds
Maintains fluid movements at high speed while turning
    Loose feeling in the body
    Edging at the top of the turn/inverse traverse
Uses knees and feet to turn the board
    Lower body pivot
    Fish turns
Uses flex of the board to create energy/acceleration
    Pump turns
    Ollies
Uses rebound for performance
    Load board in a turn allow to release - controlling the rebound and
    directing them into the next turn
Link pencil line carved turns at high speed
    Moderately steep follow the leader to set appropriate turn shape to
    control speed

LEVEL 4 - BLACK


Experiment with riding on bumpy terrain
Links turns at higher speed on blue or black
   Reduce turning corridor
   Follow the leader
   Absorb bumps by flexing lower body
   Keep board on snow


Gain confidence in advanced terrain
   Can switch between sliding and carved turn
   Can perform three flatland tricks
   Expand the nose and tail press by adding rotation


Learn about riding in icy or powder conditions
   Can adjust body position in powder
   Shift hips slightly over back foot
   Pushing on the trail
   Can relax edge angle on icy slope
   Uses pivot movements to control speed
   Lower body position

rows.label: I maintain balance on steep terrain with increased speed
I can complete short radius turns on blue & black runs
I can link turns at a higher speed on blue & black runs
I maintain fluid movements at a high speed while turning
I can switch between sliding & carved turns
I can perform three flatland tricks
I can ride in a relaxed position in powder
I can relax edge angle on icy slopes

rippers-1.name: Little Rippers · Bronze
rippers-1.guidance:
LITTLE RIPPERS - A BRONZE



Goals
    Learn to put boots on and take off
    Learn to use the bindings
    Get used to walking in boots
    Learn how to stand on the board and balance


Mobility: Technical Skills
    Help students put boots on
    Tighter or looser?
    Walking: use relays or obstacle
    Running: Freeze tag, follow the leader


Equipment: Introduce the Board and Parts
Simon Says
    Tail, nose bindings, etc.
    Explain how bindings work
    Front and back foot, toe and heelside, edge, etc.
    Rachet (alligator eating strap)
    Opening and closing strap with feet out of bindings
Yard Sale Game
    In a safe place, pile all equipment
    Have all kids run to find their board, bring it back and open their straps


Knows How to Stand on the Board to Balance
    Flat terrain strap in both feet, play head and shoulders
    Practice by towing with pole or hoops
    Being tall and small

LITTLE RIPPERS - A BRONZE



Freeride Skills
Jump 180s Board Off
   Boots on, practice jumping and spinning on flats
Nose and Tail Press (Static)
   Board on, have kids challenge themselves with new positions (after they
   have experienced sliding a bit)


Carrying the Board
   Stress putting bindings down in the snow to avoid runaways


Try to Use the Carpet with Assistance

rows.label: Equipment knowledge
rows.detail: Boots on/off; names three board parts; bindings on/off

rows.label: Balance
rows.detail: Both feet strapped in; pulled on flat terrain

rows.label: Body position
rows.detail: Tall/small while sliding; static jumps and nose/tail presses

rows.label: Lift use
Safety

rippers-2.name: Little Rippers · Silver
rippers-2.guidance:
LITTLE RIPPERS - B SILVER



Goals
   Learn about balance while sliding


Technical Skills
   Knows own equipment
   Review parts of board and boots
   Play Yard Sale


Can Stand on Board to Balance While Moving
   Start by towing with both feet attached
Minimum Terrain = Maximum Mileage
   Experimenting on safe terrain will allow kids to feel the movements
   required to adapt their body position to various speeds and slopes
Straight Running
   Safe terrain, change body positions
   Imitate an animal
   Follow a line, try grabbing nose or tail


Freeride Skills
Small Jumps
   While sliding, try two-foot jumps
Sliding nose and tail presses
   Start to have kids move their body over the tail or nose
Gliding
   Gliding with speed, the terrain should ensure speed control


Try to Use the Carpet Without Assistance

rows.label: Equipment knowledge
rows.detail: Knows own equipment; names five parts; bindings on/off

rows.label: Balance
rows.detail: Straight running with both feet strapped in

rows.label: Body position
rows.detail: Follow a line; grab nose/tail; attempt two-foot jump; sliding presses; glide with speed

rows.label: Lift use

rippers-3.name: Little Rippers · Gold
rippers-3.guidance:
LITTLE RIPPERS - C GOLD



Goals
    Improve comfort while gliding, both feet attached
    Learn to use pivot to change direction

Technical Skills
Straight Running
    Both feet attached, continue to develop balance while sliding straight
Can show three different body positions, straight running
    Fore/aft, rotational, vertical and lateral
    Use animal games, Simon Says or throw snowballs


J-Turns
    Using a hoop, pole or tether, initiate some rotation in the
    board on flat terrain
    With hands on hips and elbows out, use the lead elbow to
    direct the pivot movement
    Look in direction they want to go
    Gently direct eyes toward heelside, staring in to your eyes
    and you walk in front of them


Sliding 180s
    With assistance (hands, hoops) have students try to
    initiate the J-turn and continue to look with the eyes to
    complete a rotation on flat terrain


Can Use the Beginner Carpets Unassisted

rows.label: Equipment knowledge
rows.detail: Carries equipment; knows all board parts; bindings on/off

rows.label: Balance
Body position
rows.detail: Three positions: fore/aft, rotational, vertical or lateral

rows.label: J-turns and 180s
Lift use

devo-race.name: Devo · Race development (proposed)
devo-race.source: Meeting notes: proposed race and park report addition
devo-race.guidance: Draft observation categories for Karen and the technical team to review. No numeric pass thresholds have been approved. Follow current resort procedures, participant readiness and supervisor direction. The supplied manual requires staff park training before bringing students into the Beginner Playground. Do not treat a recorded skill as permission to enter a feature.

rows.label: Chooses a controlled line through a supervised course
Uses turn shape to manage speed
Applies balance and pressure control in a course
Explains start, finish and course safety

devo-park.source: Meeting notes: proposed race and park report addition
devo-park.guidance: Draft observation categories for Karen and the technical team to review. No numeric pass thresholds have been approved. Follow current resort procedures, participant readiness and supervisor direction. The supplied manual requires staff park training before bringing students into the Beginner Playground. Do not treat a recorded skill as permission to enter a feature.

rows.label: Recognizes feature choice and safe stopping locations
Follows supervisor guidance for entry and spacing
Maintains balance on approved introductory terrain
Describes a safe next step for practice
